access.edition_or_version: 1915 English edition; full scan verified at https://archive.org/details/onehundredpoemso00kabiuoft
access.translator: Rabindranath Tagore, assisted by Evelyn Underhill

mechanics.premise: Short, self-contained verses of a weaver-saint who attacks the apparatus of organized piety while holding fast to devotion itself.
mechanics.deflation_targets: Clerical costume and performance — the reddened robe, rosary, sacred thread, ceremonial thread-wearing, ritual bathing, idol-worship, and the wonder-working friar — all deflated as outward show (verified locators: Introduction p. xvi; Poem XXI pp. 28-29; Poems LXV-LXVII pp. 68-71; Poem LXIX pp. 72-73; described, never quoted).
mechanics.licensed_frame: The bhakti/prophetic register itself: the devotion Kabir affirms is what authorizes his ridicule of religious professionals — license earned from inside the tradition, not imported.
mechanics.point_of_view: First-person voice of the devotee-speaker, direct and unsoftened, addressing both God and the pious establishment.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Concrete material detail (garments, beads, tanks, idols) used as evidence against abstract sanctity; ironic reversal where the outward sign proves the inward fraud; no sustained institutional program — each poem is its own deflation.
mechanics.dialogue: Accusatory address to priests and pilgrims; admonition rather than conversation.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Fierce devotional certainty aimed outward at hypocrisy — anger and play coexist without ever cooling into doubt, which is why the register is irreverent rather than cynical.
mechanics.boundaries_and_restraint: Persistence against the clerical register brushes the satirical-literature boundary; what keeps it tone-irreverent is the absence of a named, sustained program-target and the preservation of the devotional core.
mechanics.conventions: Bhakti vernacular verse; anti-ritualist strain shared with other North Indian saints' traditions.
mechanics.innovation_or_subversion: Demonstrates irreverence from within devotion — sacred feeling as the engine of impiety toward the pious.
mechanics.critical_reception: The Tagore-Underhill introduction frames the tradition's piety as what Kabir denounced (p. xvi); translation-mediated reception (1915 English verse).
mechanics.audience_reception: Kabir remains among the most widely anthologized South Asian saints; this English collection is the standard historic vehicle of his reception abroad.
